title: Why won't it start?
briefing: The internal app, 'webapp', is in a failed state and the team is blocked.
Someone edited its config and now it won't come up. `systemctl start` just
fails. The journal — systemd's log — will tell you exactly why.
Read the journal, fix the config, then start it.
tips: `journalctl -u webapp` shows what webapp logged when it tried to start.
Its config lives at /etc/webapp/webapp.conf. It's root-owned — become root with `sudo -i` to edit it.
objective: Diagnose why webapp fails to start (read its journal), fix /etc/webapp/webapp.conf, and get the service active.
expert_objective: webapp is failed on app-01. Find the cause in the journal, fix it, restore the service.
hints: See the failure: `systemctl status webapp` (failed), then the reason: `journalctl -u webapp`. It names an invalid port '0' in /etc/webapp/webapp.conf.
The config is root-owned. Become root: `sudo -i`. Then set a real port, e.g. `echo "port = 8080" > /etc/webapp/webapp.conf`.
As root: `echo "port = 8080" > /etc/webapp/webapp.conf`, then `systemctl start webapp`. Status should turn active.
solution:
systemctl status webapp
journalctl -u webapp
sudo -i
echo "port = 8080" > /etc/webapp/webapp.conf
systemctl start webapp

journal: Sep 30 09:41:02 app-01 systemd[1]: Starting Internal web application...
Sep 30 09:41:02 app-01 webapp[2210]: FATAL: invalid port '0' in /etc/webapp/webapp.conf
Sep 30 09:41:02 app-01 systemd[1]: webapp.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE
Sep 30 09:41:02 app-01 systemd[1]: webapp.service: Failed with result 'exit-code'.
Sep 30 09:41:02 app-01 systemd[1]: Failed to start Internal web application.

explanation: This is the real service-debugging loop: status tells you a unit failed, the journal tells you WHY, you fix the root cause, and you start it again. A service won't magically recover — systemctl start re-reads the config, so the fix has to land in the file first.
